title: Saving energy at home
description: Lower bills and a lighter footprint start with the settings and habits you already have.

body.heading: Heat and cool the people
paragraphs: Heating and cooling usually dominate home energy use. Small setting changes — a degree or two — are barely noticeable day to day but add up across a season, and wearing a layer indoors in winter is free.
Close curtains on cold nights and on hot afternoons to keep temperatures steadier. Use fans, which cool people cheaply, before reaching for stronger cooling.

body.heading: The standby drain
paragraphs: Many devices sip power while 'off'. Switching entertainment and computer gear off at the wall, or using a power strip with one switch, trims that quiet waste without changing your life.
When appliances need replacing, energy ratings help you compare running costs, not just purchase prices — the cheaper machine can be the expensive one to run.

body.heading: Start with one room
paragraphs: Pick one room and do a mini energy audit: lights, standby devices, draughts. Success in one room shows you the pattern for the rest of the home.

takeaway: Adjust settings a degree at a time, switch standby devices fully off, and audit one room first.
